sol.section: Recommended exact spec diff: §§7.3 and 10; interaction with §14.3 T4

steps.claim: A clock read increments c, and its reversal decrements c. An eligible COMPLETED run must reverse to its entry device-model state. Section 10's ownership and reverse-eligibility conditions name registers and memory, without making the clock counter an owned resource.
steps.by: clause:ISA §7.3 clock row; clause:ISA §10 States; clause:ISA §14.3 T4

steps.claim: The amendment makes c shared by all runs of a loaded program, preserves the existing ownership conditions and expressly preserves disjoint concurrent runs.

Use two disjoint live eight-byte globals and no quantum registers. A reads the clock into its buffer and reaches COMPLETED but remains open. B reads the clock into its other buffer, completes and closes. A then reverses. No stated register/memory ownership or reverse-eligibility condition excludes this sequence.
steps.by: clause:ISA §§7.3/10; witness:ABI sequence bennett_run(A), bennett_wait(A), bennett_run(B), bennett_wait(B), bennett_run_close(B), bennett_reverse(A)

steps.claim: Starting at c=0, A leaves c=1, B leaves c=2, and A's prescribed reversal leaves c=1 rather than A's entry value 0. The analogous console sequence A writes a5, B writes 5a, close B, reverse A pops B's byte and leaves A's byte.
steps.by: witness:python3 -c 'c=0; c+=1; c+=1; c-=1; print(c)' outputs 1; clause:ISA §7.3 console and clock reversal rows

steps.claim: The amended text therefore permits an eligible reversal that contradicts its explicit entry-state restoration guarantee. Atomic effects and separate effect tapes do not isolate the shared model state.

sol.fix: In §§7.3/10, extend isolation to the newly shared models. Recommended rule: "At bennett_run, the run atomically acquires exclusive ownership of every console, clock and block model referenced by its entry's transitive CC/R call closure. Ownership lasts until CLOSED, including while COMPLETED, FAILED or REVERSED. If any required model is owned by another non-CLOSED run, bennett_run returns E_INVALID_STATE before executing the entry or acquiring ownership. Entropy positions and effect tapes remain per-run. Disjoint concurrent runs require disjoint model ownership sets as well as the existing register/memory conditions." Clarify §14.3: "Restoration concerns the run-owned state; state belonging exclusively to disjoint runs is unaffected." Add a §15 vector: after A reads clock 0 and completes without closing, B's conflicting launch returns E_INVALID_STATE, c remains 1 and B has no effects; after A closes, a new B reads 1, or reads 0 if A first reversed. A viable alternative is dynamic per-model ownership acquired at the first effect, retained until CLOSED, with a conflicting effect producing atomic terminal code 4; that alternative also needs an explicit §4.9 mapping. I recommend launch-time acquisition because it uses the existing launch-conflict status and prevents partial execution before discovering a model conflict.

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff: §§7.3/10, interacting with §7.4 and §14.3 T4

steps.claim: Console reversal pops the recorded number of bytes; clock reversal decrements c. Whole-run reversal traverses only that run's history. §10 grants exclusive ownership of registers and memory, and its reversal eligibility does not mention device interference. T4 promises device-state restoration.
steps.by: clause:ISA-7.3 device table; clause:ISA-7.4 history traversal; clause:ISA-10 States; clause:ISA-14.3 T4

steps.claim: The amendment makes console/clock/block state shared across runs of one loaded program, while retaining ownership wording limited to registers and memory and explicitly preserving disjoint concurrent runs.
steps.by: witness:docs/notes/2026-11-02-rev3/adg.md, Recommended exact spec diff, §7.3 and §10 additions

steps.claim: Use two disjoint live one-byte globals containing a5 and 5a. A's CC entry calls an R helper that writes a5 to the console, then completes but remains open. B writes 5a using its separate global, completes and closes. Neither run uses registers, measurement or unverified free. Reversing A is eligible under §10, but its one-byte pop leaves console=a5, whereas A entered with an empty console. The literal transition calculation is reproducible with the command cited here.
steps.by: witness:python3 -c 's=bytearray(); s.extend(bytes([0xa5])); s.extend(bytes([0x5a])); del s[-1:]; print(s.hex())' outputs a5

steps.claim: Thus the amended shared-state model admits a trace whose prescribed reversal contradicts T4 and removes another run's console byte. Atomic individual effects do not protect retained undo histories. The claim that no additional device synchronization rule is needed is unsound.

codex.fix: In §§7.3/10, add an explicit ownership rule. Recommended conservative wording: “A run's device ownership footprint is the set of console, clock and block models referenced by the entry's transitive CC/R call closure. bennett_run acquires that footprint exclusively before execution and retains it until CLOSED, including while COMPLETED, FAILED or REVERSED. If another non-CLOSED run owns any model in the footprint, bennett_run returns E_INVALID_STATE before execution or any ownership acquisition. Entropy position and effect tapes are run-local and do not conflict. Runs with disjoint device footprints remain subject to the existing register and memory ownership rules.” In §14.3 T4, add: “For shared program state, restoration concerns the reversing run's owned components; disjoint components belonging to other runs remain unchanged.” Add the §15 overlap vector: B's initial launch is E_INVALID_STATE with no effects; after A is reversed and closed, retried B leaves console=5a; after A is closed unreversed, retried B leaves console=a55a. A second viable approach is a specified global device-dependency history with reverse-dependency ordering for both segment uncall and whole-run reversal, accompanied by revised eligibility rules. I recommend exclusive ownership because it preserves the existing local reversal machinery.
